answer: First the comet verifier locks 64 GB of RAM and commits a Blake3 state root over the array, so a hollow copy with no real memory cannot pass. It then orders a walk of 2 million cache lines with sealed proofs due in 900 milliseconds, a mirror deadline that snaps shut on clones sharing one pool. One honest agent holds one 64 GB array; 10 fakes must hold 640 GB on ten buses, about $4,800. Peers replay the walk and slash the bond of mismatched proofs, freezing repeat offenders, so no cedar faker can fake memory it never locked.
